data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumption is governed by case-matched evidence: the permissibility depends on which of four exhaustive cases the exhaustion falls into\u2014(A) inter-event boundary, (B) intra-event but extra-checksum-verified, (C) intra-event with ambiguous framing, (D) intra-event with detected corruption\u2014and only cases A and B permit resumption while C and D require refusal.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The four cases are not exhaustive\u2014there exists a fifth case, e.g., exhaustion at a framing boundary where the boundary marker itself is corrupted, bridging C and D.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Case B is impossible in practice because checksums always cover complete records only, so a truncated record's checksum is never verifiable.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The distinction between C and D collapses when the framing protocol provides no integrity check at all, making corruption undetectable and all intra-event truncations look like case C.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Anchoring in cases: Case A is the trivial safe case\u2014the truncation falls on a clean record boundary, resumption appends next events, both invariants hold. Case B: truncation is intra-event but the event carries an end-of-record checksum that the resumption protocol can test; if the checksum-verified prefix is a complete event, quarantine the suffix and resume; if not, the record is partial and must be treated per case C. Case C: framing is ambiguous (length-prefix truncated, no checksum), so the protocol cannot deterministically decide whether the last bytes constitute a partial or complete event\u2014resumption would risk logical corruption, so refuse. Case D: integrity checks reveal corruption within what framing marks as a complete event\u2014physical append-only identity itself is threatened, so refuse and require audit. This four-case partition adjudicates between the mechanist (who collapses to 'always A') and the skeptic (who collapses to 'always C/D').","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
